_why: Which of the estate's root-level games can carry /hud.js is not derivable from the games. Ten of the twenty-three ship under a contract their own verifier enforces: a single self-contained HTML file with no external script, no remote subresource, and in two cases a pinned byte ledger or source SHA. Adding <script src="/hud.js"> to one of those is not a mechanical edit that happens to trip a check - it retracts a promise the game makes. So the exclusions are declared here, with the verifier and the gate that would go red, in the same class as gameIdOverrides, canonicalAliases, reclassifyAsGame and chooserLinkText.
_measured: 2026-08-10. Each entry was measured, not assumed: the game's verifier was run on the unmodified tree (green), the script line was inserted, and the verifier was run again. Only gates that turned from green to red are listed. Nothing here is a guess about what a verifier might say.
_precedent: /neonbreach/ carries the script and passes, because tools/verify_neonbreach.js was deliberately amended when it was added: it asserts only-same-origin-src-is-hud, three-script-blocks and third-block-is-hud-loader. That is what admitting the HUD to a single-file game costs - a considered amendment to that game's contract, one game at a time. Doing it for eight more is a product decision about eight games' self-contained promise, and it is not this pass's to take.
_consequence: A visitor playing one of these eight has the browser Back button and the game's own navigation, and no HUD back control or chosen-homepage control. That is the status quo for all eight, not a regression introduced here.
_scope: THIS LEDGER GOVERNS 23 OF 62, AND NO CHECK IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN SEE THE OTHER 39. The canonical inventory - data/mbm-search-index.json - holds 62 game routes: 23 single-segment routes served from this repository, and 39 under /Lessons/ served from MattRoper1977/Lessons. The split is exact, with no route in neither group. verify_hud_on_games.py asserts that every inventory game is wired or declared and nothing in between; read without this note, that reads estate-wide, and it is not - it is true of the 23. The Lessons 39, and the 3 exclusions among them, are governed by that repository's own data/hud-coverage.json. Neither repository contains the other's files, so neither tool could judge the other half even if it wanted to. The only place a single check could see all 58 is the cross-estate job, which is the one job that checks out both estates and assembles them onto one origin; no such check exists today, and this note is here so the absence is stated rather than inferred from a number that looks complete. COUNTS RE-MEASURED 2026-08-15: the prose above previously read "19 of 58", "nineteen" and "Eight", which had gone stale as games shipped. data/mbm-search-index.json now holds 62 game routes - 23 single-segment served from this repository and 39 under /Lessons/ - and this ledger lists 10 exclusions. verify_hud_on_games.py reports the same split from the index at run time, so the numbers in this prose are the ones that rot; if they disagree with the tool, the tool is right.

gates: G1 single file, single script, no dependency

inlineExitRegion._what: An inline exit control, stamped byte-identically into every game declared here. No src, no dependency, no request: the single-file promise these games make is intact. Generated by the site repository's tools/render_inline_exit.py, never hand-written - eleven hand-copies of one control is one literal repeated eleven times.
inlineExitRegion._why: The consequence recorded above - browser Back and nothing else - is not survivable on a locked-down school device, where the browser chrome may not be there at all. A child finishing echovault or relicforge had no way out of the page. Amending eight more verifiers to admit <script src="/hud.js"> was the alternative, and the precedent cited for it is /neonbreach/, whose amendment let in a script that then rendered nothing for months and nobody looked. Inline costs bytes and moves ledgers; it retracts no promise.
inlineExitRegion._rendered: Proven in a browser, not in source, by the site repository's tools/verify_inline_exit.mjs: present in the DOM, at least 44x44 px as rendered, resolving a real href, on top where a finger lands and keyboard-reachable, for all eleven at 390, 768 and 1440 px. R-HUC01 - a text search over source is evidence about the text, never about the runtime.
inlineExitRegion._generator: tools/render_inline_exit.py (site repository); --check asserts every stamped region is byte-identical to a freshly generated one
inlineExitRegion._stripper: tools/mbm_exit_region.js, emitted into both repositories by the same generator, so the gates that judge a game's own contract remove the platform's region first

_emberwild: /emberwild/ is NOT excluded, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight - see issue MattRoper1977/mattroper1977.github.io#149. It carries the inline exit region and no /hud.js, so verify_hud_on_games.py is red on it (15 assertions: wired-or-declared, the script count, and back/home controls at 320/768/1440). Adding it here would turn that green and is the wrong repair. This ledger's own _measured rule admits an entry only when inserting the script line turns one of the game's gates from green to red; measured on 2026-08-15 against emberwild/index.html (c8641d81..., 306480 B -> 9c17eacb..., 306518 B), NOTHING turned red - tools/verify_emberwild.js and tools/verify_emberwild_bayer.mjs both scored identically to the clean file. Emberwild has no contract objection to the HUD, so the repair is to wire it, not to declare it. Do not close the red by adding a route here.
